title: Bitwidth Impact Oracle and Autotune Recommender for Hybrid AWQ/GPTQ
creator: Diego Marques
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'Bitwidth Impact Oracle' and a complementary 'Autotune Recommender' that (a) estimates per-route and per-cohort quality risk when switching to mixed/hybrid quantization (AWQ/GPTQ, int8/int4), and (b) suggests safe threshold and rollout parameters for deployment. This ticket focuses on the evaluation harness, gating heuristics, and the first-pass recommender prototype integrated into the CI/evals pipeline.

Background: We have multiple manual analyses showing that some cohorts (short prompts, code generation, multi-turn chat) are more sensitive to low-bit quantization than others. Current processes require engineers to run bespoke test suites and eyeball delta heatmaps. This work creates an automated oracle that translates model/config deltas into concrete rollout recommendations (e.g., quantize to int8 with layerwise exceptions; pin AWQ for decoder-only layers; set fidelity gate at KL>0.015 per-cohort). The autotune recommender will compute a suggested threshold and a staged rollout plan (canary size, fallback model, monitoring hooks).

Scope & Deliverables:
- Evaluation harness adapter that runs AWQ and GPTQ variants on a canonical cohort set (chat, Q&A, code, summarization) and computes per-cohort metrics: ROUGE/BLEU/accuracy, semantic-similarity delta, and a calibrated regression score.
- A 'risk oracle' function that maps metric deltas and distributional features to a single risk score and categorical recommendation (Safe | Review | Block).
- Autotune recommender that produces: suggested bitwidth profile, per-layer exception list (if required), fidelity threshold, and canary rollout parameters (percent, sampling strategy, monitoring hooks).
- Integration with CI: automated job that runs on model/config PRs and posts a structured report to PRs (comment + link to eval dashboard).
- Documentation and runbook for SRE/Oncall: how to interpret the report and manually override recommendations.

Non-goals: Full production rollout automation, RBAC controls for automatic rollouts, and deep model fine-tuning to recover regression. Those will be separate follow-ups.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run AWQ and GPTQ variants for at least 3 canonical cohorts and produce reproducible delta metrics.
- Oracle produces a risk score consistent with manual review on 10 historical regression cases (>= 80% agreement).
- Recommender outputs actionable rollout parameters and a suggested fallback path.
- CI integration posts a human-readable summary to PRs and links to the detailed dashboard.
- Runbook created and reviewed by the SRE and ML research leads.

2026-03-02 ML Research (Lena Hofmann): Provided labeled historical regression set (10 incidents) and guidance for mapping semantic delta to user-visible impact. Added Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/bitwidth-risk-guidelines

2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Risk oracle v0 implemented. Uses weighted combination of token-level KL, embedding cosine drop, and task-specific metric delta. Tuned initial weights to match historical cases (7/10 agreement). Push: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-evals/commit/7c9a2f

2026-03-06 Diego Marques: Review feedback: oracle too conservative for code cohort. Action: add cohort-specific scaling and incorporate prefix-length distribution as a feature. Filed follow-up ENG-445679 for cohort profiling improvements.

2026-03-08 Aisha Patel: Autotune recommender prototype outputs: bitwidth suggestion, layer exception list heuristics (exclude final LM head if delta large), and simple canary plan (5% seeds from low-risk cohorts). Example PR comment format added to CI job. See sample report: https://internal-dashboards.redwood.ai/bitwidth-oracle/reports/ENG-445678-sample

2026-03-10 Diego Marques: Ran end-to-end on three candidate model/config PRs. Agreement with manual reviewers improved to 8/10 after cohort scaling. Preparing runbook draft and test checklist for SRE review. Next: expand cohort set and calibrate thresholds (target 9/10 agreement).
